items.title: feat(ci): scout classifier leg on the main-broken chain (#2176)
items.body: Implements the CI-failure classifier (scout) leg of issue #2176's failure-triage design on code's main-broken chain — queue task 13485. ## What lands - **`scripts/classify_failure.py`** (new, stdlib-only): reads the log tails of a failed run's failing jobs and classifies the breakage as `quota-or-secret` / `infra-runner` / `infra-network` / `flake-suspect` / `real-regression` / `unknown`, emitting JSON with up to 5 evidence lines and a route. Rule order is part of the contract: quota/runner/network signals beat a generic failing-test summary from the same job. - **`main-broken.yml` scout step pair** between filing and remediation: - classifies from the failing jobs' log tails and posts an `agent-note:v1` with the classification + evidence on the breakage issue **before any fix spend**; - routing per the design: quota/secret → escalate (label + note naming the implicated credential, zero fix attempts); infra/flake → one automatic re-run of the failed jobs (`run_attempt` guard; a repeat escalates as infrastructure; third flake strike files a deduped flake-fix issue); real-regression/unknown → existing Jules/queue routing with the diagnosis attached; - the `jules`-label step and the append-path fix-task dispatch now gate on the scout route (empty route = scout silence = previous behaviour, fail-open); - `workflow_dispatch dry_run=true` prints the classification and files/sends nothing (the route step is create/append-only). - **Tests**: 18 contract tests in `scripts/tests/test_classify_failure.py` (one fixture family per class, rule-ordering, evidence cap, tail-window behaviour), wired into `scripts-test.yml`. ## Verification - `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_classify_failure.py'` — 18/18 pass on the laptop worktree. - `actionlint .github/workflows/main-broken.yml .github/workflows/scripts-test.yml` — clean. - Classifier CLI smoke test against a fabricated failed-job log dir + jobs manifest → `infra-network` / route `rerun` with the DNS line as evidence. - The live `workflow_dispatch dry_run=true` run against a known failed run can only execute once this workflow is on the default branch (GitHub dispatches the default-branch workflow definition); that is the first post-merge validation step. Scope guardrails preserved: no `workflow_run` on `*`, per-breakage concurrency unchanged, scout authority limited to one re-run + comment/label/file within chain labels; it never edits code, merges, touches secrets, or disables workflows. Issue #2176 stays open (other jewels/bullets are separate packets). Refs #2176 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **CI & Reliability** * Failed checks are now categorized as infrastructure, intermittent, or code-related failures, with relevant log evidence captured for review. * Infrastructure and intermittent failures can be rerun automatically; quota or secret-related failures can be escalated. * Issues are routed based on failure type, and the fix queue is updated only when a fix task is queued.

items.title: feat(workflows): agents thin caller, in-CI ci-fix hook, pm-dispatch smoke (#2672)
items.body: Part of #2672 Per-repo integration (parts 5/5b/7) for `developing-today/code`: the repo's scheduled agents become a thin caller of the central reusable workflow, CI failures dispatch a fixer from inside the failing run, and a standing smoke workflow proves pm-dispatch-task's ci-fix mode. ## Per-file summary - **NEW `.github/workflows/agents.yml`** — the repo's single home for dispatch-scheduled agents (Bolt/Palette/Suggestions, replacing the retired Jules scheduled tasks + Suggestions), as a THIN CALLER of the central reusable workflow (shape correction 2026-10-30 06:06 CDT — no per-task steps). Triggers: `schedule` with exactly two crons (tasks `0 1 * * *`, suggestions `0 13 * * *`) and `workflow_dispatch` with a `task` choice input (all/bolt/palette/suggestions, default all). Permissions `id-token: write, contents: read` (workflow- and job-level). Exactly one job, `scheduled`, a reusable-workflow call to `developing-today/code/.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml@main` (no `runs-on`, no steps) passing `schedule: ${{ github.event.schedule }}` and `tasks:` as an expression that is empty on schedule events and when the selector is `all`, and the selector value on a specific manual pick; `repo` is omitted (the central workflow defaults it from the caller context). Header comment records the thin-caller shape, that the task list / slot table / prompts live centrally (`pm-scheduled.yml` + the pm-dispatch-task prompt library in this repo — edit them there, not here), and the time conversion: crons are UTC converted from America/Chicago CDT (tasks 20:00, suggestions 08:00); during CST the local fire time shifts one hour earlier. - **`.github/workflows/nix-ci.yml` (main CI — ci-fix hook)** — additive only: a new `ci-fix` job that `needs: [proxy-port-fallbacks, flake-check]`, runs only `if: failure()`, with permissions `id-token: write, issues: read, contents: read` on `ubuntu-latest`, whose single step calls `developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-ci-fix@main` with `continue-on-error: true` and `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` in the step env. No `with:` block — the wrapper defaults all ci-fix context from this run. - **Main-CI pick: `nix-ci.yml` ("nix ci"), main jobs `proxy-port-fallbacks` + `flake-check`.** Why: it is the repo's only repo-wide CI workflow — no path filter, runs on push to main + `merge_group` + nightly schedule; per `.github/ci-policy.md` its `basic: proxy port fallbacks` job is the repo's sole required status check / merge-queue gate and its `flake-check` job is the full main-tier flake evaluation. Every other candidate is path-gated to a single package (`id` → pkgs/id only, `mcpx` / `mcpx conformance` / `mcpx nix build` → pkgs/mcpx only, `go modules build`, `identity build`, `map build`, `lab-ops-hub`, etc.). Existing structure/style preserved. - **`.github/workflows/jules.yml`** — removed the `ci-failure-fix` job (the workflow_run-triggered CI-failure fixer that part 3 / PR #2678 converted to a pm-dispatch-start call; verified from the file: its `if:` keys on `github.event.workflow_run` failure and it dispatched a "CI failure: …" fix session). It is superseded by the in-CI `ci-fix` job in nix-ci.yml (the fixer hooks inside the failing run; no workflow_run design). The `workflow_run` trigger went with it — it existed only for that job (its own comment says so) — and a brief comment where the job was notes the move. All other jobs (`weekly-cleanup`, `issue-labeled`, `manual`) and the schedule/issues/workflow_dispatch triggers are untouched. - **NEW `.github/workflows/pm-dispatch-smoke.yml`** — workflow_dispatch-only standing proof for pm-dispatch-task's ci-fix mode. One job (`smoke`; permissions `id-token: write, issues: read, contents: read`) with one step calling `developing-today/code/.github/actions/pm-dispatch-task@main` with `task: ci-fix`, `workflow: "ci-fix smoke"`, `run-id: "0"`, `run-url: "https://example.invalid/ci-fix-smoke"`, `branch: main`, `sha: ${{ github.sha }}`, and `GH_TOKEN` in the env. Header comment states the context is fabricated and clearly a smoke test, and the expected behaviour: a first run creates the issue `ci-fix: ci-fix smoke failing on main` plus a claimed task and a session via the starter path; a repeat run attaches a second task to the same issue (dedupe); results are cleaned up manually after proof runs. This PR does NOT dispatch it (the coordinator runs the proof). No changes under `nixos/**`, `pm-stack/**`, or to any secrets. (This branch also contains a merge of current `main`, which is how the already-merged pm-dispatch-ci-fix wrapper from #2701 enters the branch's history — no pm-stack edits were made by this PR's own commit.) ## Validation - All four touched workflows parse with `python3 yaml.safe_load` (the `on:` → bool artifact is the known PyYAML quirk). - Structural checks passed: agents.yml has exactly one job (`scheduled`), no `runs-on`/`steps` on it, no `workflow_run` trigger, and exactly the two specified crons; the smoke workflow is workflow_dispatch-only with one job / one step; nix-ci's `ci-fix` has the specified needs/if/permissions/step; jules.yml no longer contains `ci-failure-fix` or a `workflow_run` trigger and keeps its other three jobs. - `actionlint` is not installed on either the sandbox or the laptop, so it could not be run. ## Merge gate Per the #2672 coordination rules this PR merges only after BOTH `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-ci-fix@main` (landed in #2701) and `.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml@main` exist on main. If the latter is not yet on main when this PR is otherwise ready, it stays open as ready-to-merge for the coordinator. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added twice-daily scheduled task runs, with manual options to run all tasks or select a specific task. * CI failures can now trigger an automated fix workflow. * Added a manually run smoke test for the dispatch process; it may create test issues and tasks that require cleanup. * **Changes** * Removed the previous automatic fix run triggered by completed CI workflows.

items.title: mcpx: preflight import-graph report stage (#1915 stage 1)
items.body: Stage 1 (Graph) of #1915, report slice — queue task 3194. **What this adds** - `internal/preflight/imports.go`: a new preflight stage beside `script.typecheck`. It runs `deno info --json` on the launcher, parses the graph (`ParseGraph`), and reports **every** unresolved specifier in one pass with the as-written specifier and its source span in the importer (`ReportGraph`, extending the `TestEveryBadPathIsReportedInOnePass` shape). Missing modules are joined back to their importing edge from deno's error entries, so spans survive. - Computed dynamic `import()`/`require()` — the edges the graph cannot contain — are detected by scanning the source of every local module in the graph and surfaced per `script.importsOnDynamic` (`warn|fail|ignore`, default `warn`), naming script and span. Never silently ignored. - Settings in the one registry: `script.imports` (`off|report`, default `report`) and `script.importsOnDynamic` (`warn|fail|ignore`, default `warn`). `script.imports=off` disables the stage entirely. Wired through the CLI script shape, the local runner path, `execsvc` (wire options + limits) and the daemon limits, mirroring how `script.typecheck` flows, so local and remote runs agree. - Remote-exec degradation (documented in `CheckImportsText`): a script that arrives as text has no file graph, so only its visible top-level bare specifiers are analysed — reported as *unverifiable*, not missing — plus its computed dynamic imports. - Generated docs regenerated (`configuration.md`, `environment.md`, `parity.md`). **Explicitly out of scope** (stays on #1915): the Prepare stage and `script.importsOnMissing` / `importsCrossProject` / `importsNetwork` — they depend on #1908's cache mechanism and #1913's resolved dependency set. No installs, no cache writes, no writes into any project directory in this slice. **Verification** - New unit tests: deno-info fixture parsing (fixture shape captured from deno 2.9.7 against a script with two missing imports), one-pass missing-specifier report, computed dynamic import warn/fail/ignore, literal dynamic imports not flagged, `off` is a no-op, missing-deno is a warning not a failure, text-mode bare specifiers. - Live check on the laptop with real deno: `CheckImports` on a script with a missing import + a computed dynamic import → fatal report naming `./missing-a.ts`, warning for the computed edge. - Laptop `go test`: preflight, runner, execsvc, daemon, cli all pass. `internal/settings` has two failures (`TestEveryDocumentHasAChapter`, `TestTheReadByColumnIsWhatTheCodeReads`) that also fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree — pre-existing, untouched by this change. Refs #1915 (stage 1 of it; the issue stays open for Resolve/Prepare). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Script runs can now check the import graph before execution and report unresolved imports. This check is configurable and defaults to reporting issues. * Computed dynamic imports can now be configured to produce a warning, fail the run, or be ignored; the default is to warn. * Import-check settings are applied to both local and remote script execution. * **Documentation** * Added documentation for the import-check settings and their command-line and environment-variable options.
